level: master (laurea magistrale / 2nd cycle) — 120 ECTS over 2 years (4 semesters), Italian degree class LM-65, Faculty of Design and Art. The fourth semester is dedicated entirely to research and the development of the final project: 'In the fourth semester, you develop a final project as your master's degree. You can choose your project. Your work is overseen by a thesis supervisor and a co-supervisor. You present and discuss it in front of a commission.' The final exam is worth 19 CP — an unusually large thesis weighting for a unibz master (compare 11 CP at the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance), consistent with a practice-based art/design degree.
teaching_language: FULLY ENGLISH — a genuinely monolingual English programme, not a trilingual one. The admission-information PDF states without qualification: 'The official teaching language is English.' The 'At a glance' box on both the programme page and the brochure says 'Courses will be taught in: English'. This is confirmed course by course: every single course published on the 2026/27 course-offering page carries the language code EN — Studio 1 (Natures-Cultures: Research based Art and Design; Ecocriticism), Studio 2 (Critical Environments; Histories and Theories of Spatial Practices), Studio 3 (Techno-Human-Expressions; Art Theories), Design & Materials, Design & Production, Information Design and Visual Storytelling, Spatial Design, Human Computer Interaction, Interaction and Communication Design, Environmental Anthropology, Social Studies of Design and Culture, Media Studies, Gender Studies, Postcolonial Studies, Histories of Science and Technologies, Histories Theories and Critical Interpretations of Art, Policy Design Democracy and Citizen Engagement, Project Development and Sustainability, Seminar in Software Engineering Advances and Seminar 2: Academic Writing. There is no Italian-taught or German-taught curricular subject. THE ONE EXCEPTION is a single mandatory 3 CP 'Language Course (Italian or German)' in the second year, with the rule: 'Students must choose one of the two language courses offered, other than the language of the highschool diploma.' This is a taught language course inside the study plan, not a CEFR certification gate and not a condition of admission. Consequently the entry language requirement is English B2 and nothing else — there is no C1+B2 two-language rule and no third language.
campus: Bozen-Bolzano — the main city-centre campus, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. Faculty of Design and Art Secretariat at the same address, +39 0471 015000, design-art@unibz.it (opening hours Mon and Wed 10:00-12:00, Thu 14:00-16:00, Tue and Fri online only 10:00-12:00). No teaching at NOI Techpark, Brixen-Bressanone, Bruneck-Brunico, Trento or Innsbruck. The Faculty of Design and Art's physical infrastructure is central to this programme: 'Ateliers are dynamic and collaborative workspaces designed to foster the exchange of ideas between students and supervisors', and the technical workshops are 'equipped with state-of-the-art facilities' and 'Skilled professionals manage our workshops'. Workshop attendance is compulsory and is gated by mandatory safety training (Work Safety - Machinery Hazard - Chemical Risk), so this is a physically campus-bound, studio-based degree with no distance or hybrid variant. Documented off-campus activity includes visits such as the 'Feedback. The Environments of Franco Vaccari' exhibition at Museion (Bolzano's museum of modern and contemporary art) and a performance workshop with Vivien Tauchmann.
degree_class: LM-65 — Scienze dello spettacolo e produzione multimediale (Performing Arts and Multimedia Production). Stated identically in the 'At a glance' box of the programme page and of the brochure: 'Degree class: LM-65'. 120 ECTS, 2 years. IMPORTANT DOCUMENT DEFECT, recorded so a reader does not mistake it for real information: unibz's boilerplate sentence on simultaneous enrolment carries a DIFFERENT class code in each document and neither matches LM-65. majors_tracks_study_plans:

This distinguishes it from the Faculty of Design and Art's bachelor, which is split into a Major in Art and a Major in Design. There is no dual-study version, no four-year variant, no distance or hybrid mode, and no published part-time option.

english_only_accessibility:
OPEN — one of the most accessible unibz masters for a candidate whose only language is English, and the exact opposite of the trilingual programmes. The entry language rule is a single line: 'The official teaching language is English ... Entry level (to gain admission) — English: B2.' There is no Italian or German entry requirement, no C1+B2 two-language rule, no third language, and — unlike every trilingual unibz degree — NO exit language requirement is published at all. A candidate with a B2 English certificate, or an English-medium bachelor (recognised as C1), clears the language gate outright.

The only Italian/German element is the mandatory 3 CP 'Language Course (Italian or German)' in year 2, which must differ from the language of the applicant's high-school diploma. For a Turkish applicant whose diploma is in Turkish, either language may be chosen and the course starts from whatever level the Language Centre places them at; it is a curricular course to attend and pass, not a CEFR level to certify, and it does not affect admission.

HARD EVIDENCE THAT THE LANGUAGE GATE IS SOFT HERE: across both published 2026/27 ranking lists only TWO applicants in total were excluded for failing the language requirement (Applicant IDs 154425 and 131067, Early Bird, EU pool), and the Late list records no language exclusions in its named categories. Compare the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance, where sixteen applicants were excluded on language grounds in the same cycle.

WHERE THE REAL BARRIERS ARE, for an English-only international applicant: (1) DISCIPLINARY ELIGIBILITY — you must hold an art / design / architecture / planning / literature / philosophy degree or have accumulated 12 credit points in Design, Architecture, Arts, Museology, Cinema, Photography, Media Studies or Philosophy; a candidate from an unrelated field is excluded on 'study title' regardless of language. (2) THE NON-EU QUOTA — only 5 places, filled exactly in 2026/27 out of 21 ranked non-EU applicants, with a cut-off sitting on the 60/100 floor. (3) THE PORTFOLIO AND PROJECT PROPOSAL — a creative-practice dossier that half the Early Bird applicants failed to get above 30/60. VERDICT: open. Language is not the obstacle; discipline, portfolio quality and the small non-EU quota are.
admission_type:
RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato) with a TWO-STAGE, 100-POINT SELECTION combining documentary evaluation and a compulsory online interview. Quoted: 'The admission procedure includes 2 stages, candidates can gain a maximum score of 100 points.' STAGE 1 — evaluation of documents, max 60 points, split CV 20 / Portfolio 20 / Outline of a project proposal 20, with an eliminatory gate: 'Candidates must achieve a minimum score of 30/60 total points in Stage 1, in order to be admitted to Stage 2.' STAGE 2 — 'an online interview aimed at having a dialogue to gain a deeper understanding on the candidate's ideas, experiences and points of view', max 40 points, approximately 15 minutes. FINAL GATE: 'Candidates must achieve a minimum score of 60/100 total points to be eligible for the enrolment.' Separate ranking lists and separate quotas for (i) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (ii) non-EU citizens living abroad.

WHAT IS NOT USED: no entrance examination, no TOLC-I / TOLC-E, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT, no GRE, no written admission test, no motivation letter, no video, no reference letters, no Webometrics ranking bonus, no grade-average score and no minimum grade average. Prior academic performance carries NO direct points at all — the bachelor's final grade is used only to check eligibility, and academic background feeds the selection only indirectly through the CV criterion ('the consistence of the previous academic career with the contents of the course'). The only test-like element anywhere in the process is the optional English B2 exam at the unibz Language Centre, and only for applicants who use that route to prove their level rather than a certificate or an English-medium qualification.
academic_requirements:

ROUTE 2 — a Diploma Accademico di primo livello of the 'Accademie di Belle Arti' or of the 'Istituti Superiori per le Industrie Artistiche', in one of: DAPL03 Scuola di decorazione; DAPL04 Scuola di grafica; DAPL05 Scuola di scenografia; DAPL06 Scuola di progettazione artistica per l'impresa; DAPL08 Scuola di nuove tecnologie dell'arte; DIPL01 Scuola di progettazione grafica ed editoriale; DIPL02 Scuola di Design.

ROUTE 3 — another ITALIAN degree plus 12 credit points in these scientific disciplinary sectors 'or in equivalent subjects of the Accademia di Belle Arti or of the Istituti Superiori per le Industrie Artistiche': ICAR/13 Industrial Design; ICAR/14 Architectural and Urban Composition; ICAR/15 Landscape Design; ICAR/17 Representation of Architecture; ICAR/18 History of Architecture; L-ART/03 History of Contemporary Art; L-ART/04 Museology, art and restoration criticism; L-ART/05 Performing arts; L-ART/06 Cinema, photography and television; M-FIL/04 Aesthetics; M-FIL/05 Philosophy and theory of language. NOTE: these are the OLD (pre-2024) SSD codes; the admission documents have not been updated to the 2024-reform codes, whereas the course offering already uses the new ones (CEAR-08/D, ARTE-01/C, PHIL-04/A etc.). The new-code equivalents of the listed sectors are broadly CEAR-08/D (ex ICAR/13), CEAR-09/C (ex ICAR/14), CEAR-10/A (ex ICAR/15), CEAR-11/A (ex ICAR/18), ARTE-01/C (ex L-ART/03), PHIL-04/A (ex M-FIL/04) and PHIL-05/A (ex M-FIL/05).

ROUTE 4 — THE ROUTE MOST FOREIGN APPLICANTS USE. Quoted: 'a bachelor degree, university diploma or equivalent degree of another class or study qualifications earned abroad can be valued as adequate if, during your study career and before the beginning of the admission procedure, you have gained 12 credit points in the following fields: Design, Architecture, Arts, Museology, Cinema, Photography, Media Studies or Philosophy. A commission checks the validity and equivalence of the credit points.' Two features make this materially easier than the equivalent rule at the Faculty of Economics masters: the threshold is 12 ECTS, not 16, and the credits do NOT have to be spread across two or more disciplinary areas — 12 credits concentrated in a single field such as Media Studies qualify. The fields are also named in plain language rather than by SSD code, which gives the commission room to accept foreign coursework that has no Italian SSD equivalent. The credits must have been gained BEFORE the admission procedure begins.

ENROLMENT-STAGE VOLUME REQUIREMENT: the Diploma Supplement must show 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'.

NOT YET GRADUATED: permitted, with NO minimum ECTS threshold published — see conditional_admission. NO MINIMUM GRADE AVERAGE is set, and no grade-based score exists. NATIONAL RULE: 'simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is possible (however, the two programmes must not belong to the same class ... and must differ for at least 2/3 of the course contents).' CREDIT RECOGNITION: 'Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.'
entry_exam_or_test:

EXAM FORMAT (B2). Duration approximately 155 minutes, entirely computer-based and taken remotely, in three modules: Module I listening comprehension (2 audio clips of 5-6 minutes) plus reading comprehension and language in use (2 texts of 600-700 words), 80 minutes; Module II written production, one text of approximately 280 words chosen from two topics, 60 minutes; Module III oral production, 2 monologues with 3 minutes preparation and 2.5 minutes speaking each, 15 minutes. 'To pass the entire exam ... you must achieve in all three modules at least 60% of the allocated points.' 'If you pass Module I, you will automatically be admitted to Modules II and III. Candidates who fail Module I cannot proceed to Modules II and III.' Passed modules carry over: 'Candidates who pass Module I have to pass Modules II and III within eighteen months after having passed Module I.' Results are uploaded to the application portal 'within 10 days at the latest'. A one-shot mock test of Module I is available after registration. A PC or notebook is required (Windows 10/11 or macOS 10.15+, 8 GB RAM, 2 Mbit/s) plus a mobile device running the Zoom app; tablets and phones cannot run the exam platform. Valid photo ID must be shown at check-in. 'It is not possible to take exams at different levels for the same language.'
selection_scoring:
MAXIMUM 100 POINTS ACROSS TWO STAGES, WITH TWO ELIMINATORY THRESHOLDS.

STAGE 1 — DOCUMENTS, MAX 60 POINTS.
• Curriculum vitae, in English, PDF — max 20 points. Criterion: 'Will be evaluated the consistence of the previous academic career with the contents of the course and significant experiences not included in academic training.' Note the second half: non-academic practice (exhibitions, residencies, studio work, publications, activism, freelance projects) is explicitly scoreable.
• Portfolio, in English, PDF, max file size 20 MB — max 20 points. Criteria: 'Consistence of the projects with the contents of the course; Observational and judgment skills; Innovative and creative thinking; Formal qualities of the portfolio in relation to artistic and design production.'
• Outline of a project proposal, PDF, maximum two A4 pages — max 20 points. Criteria: 'Consistence with the contents of the course; Observational and judgment skills; Innovative and creative thinking.'
ELIMINATORY GATE: 'Candidates must achieve a minimum score of 30/60 total points in Stage 1, in order to be admitted to Stage 2.' 'Based on the documents received, the commission will decide which applicants will be admitted to the second stage of the admission process.'

STAGE 2 — INTERVIEW, MAX 40 POINTS. Criteria: 'Interdisciplinary interest; Communication skills; Creative abilities of the candidates.' Content: portfolio, CV and project proposal; general questions on design and/or art in relation to the specifics of the programme; experience already acquired in the field of study; inter- and transdisciplinary experiences; innovative and creative thinking; 'Ability to discuss and reflect critically.'
FINAL GATE: 'Candidates must achieve a minimum score of 60/100 total points to be eligible for the enrolment.'

TIE-BREAK, in order: '1. Score obtained for the interview; 2. Sum of the scores obtained for the portfolio and curriculum vitae; 3. Score obtained for the outline of a project proposal. Only in the case of further ties, the younger candidate will be preferred.' The interview therefore breaks ties before any document score — a further sign of how much weight the commission places on the live conversation.

ACTUAL 2026/27 COMPETITION, from the two signed ranking lists.
EARLY BIRD, EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS ENJOYING PARITY OF TREATMENT: 8 admitted against 20 places — the quota was NOT filled. Scores 99, 85, 80, 80, 77, 76, 64, 60; cut-off exactly 60, i.e. the eliminatory floor itself. A further 8 EU applicants failed Stage 1 with scores 27, 26, 22, 22, 20, 20, 20 and 17 out of 60; 2 EU applicants were excluded on language.
EARLY BIRD, NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD: 5 admitted against 5 places — the quota was EXACTLY filled. Scores 78, 71, 64, 60, 60; the fourth and fifth admits sat precisely on the 60-point floor. A further 5 non-EU applicants reached the interview but missed the floor with 51, 50, 47, 44 and 36; another 11 failed Stage 1 with 25, 23, 23, 21, 21, 20, 20, 18, 17, 16 and 13. So 21 non-EU applicants were ranked and 5 were admitted — roughly a 24% success rate, and both marginal admits would have failed with one point less.
LATE APPLICATION, EU/PARITY: 9 admitted. Scores 80, 77, 74 (provisionally admitted, bachelor not yet concluded), 72, 71, 70, 70, 60, 60. One applicant excluded for not reaching the minimum score, with 30. No non-EU section exists in the Late list.
RUNNING TOTAL for 2026/27 across the two published sessions: 17 EU/parity and 5 non-EU admitted, against 30 EU and 5 non-EU places.

THREE READINGS THAT MATTER FOR AN APPLICANT.
(1) THE EU POOL IS SOFT, THE NON-EU POOL IS HARD. Twelve of the twenty Early Bird EU places went unused and a third session had to be opened, while the non-EU quota filled exactly and eliminated three quarters of its ranked applicants. Establishing parity of treatment moves a candidate from the second regime to the first.
(2) STAGE 1 IS WHERE MOST APPLICANTS DIE, AND THE SCORES ARE BIMODAL. Every Stage 1 failure across both pools scored between 13 and 27 out of 60, while every admitted candidate scored 60 to 99 out of 100. There is almost no middle. That pattern is characteristic of thin or off-brief dossiers — missing or generic portfolios, project proposals that ignore the set question — rather than of narrowly-lost competition.
(3) REAPPLYING WORKS, AND THE DOCUMENTS ARE THE VARIABLE. Three Applicant IDs appear in both 2026/27 lists. ID 155609 scored 22/60 at Stage 1 in the Early Bird and was excluded, then scored 72/100 in the Late session and was admitted at rank 4. ID 151042 went from 27/60 and exclusion to 60/100 and admission at rank 9. ID 152266 scored 77 in both sessions (rank 5 Early Bird, rank 2 Late). Since neither the academic record nor any bonus can change between March and June, the only thing that moved was the quality of the CV, portfolio, project proposal and interview. unibz explicitly invites this: 'They may re-apply in the second session.'

SELECTION COMMISSION, which changed between sessions: EARLY BIRD — President Prof. Roberto Gigliotti (the degree course director), Member Prof. Shona Kitchen. LATE APPLICATION — President Prof. Davide Tommaso Maria Pierfelice Ferrando, Member Prof. Matilde Cassani. Both decrees are digitally signed.
bonus_points:
NONE. This programme has no bonus-point mechanism of any kind, and that absence is itself important because it makes the rubric unusually flat and unusually controllable by the applicant. There is NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that belongs to the Faculty of Engineering masters — Software Engineering and Computing for Data Science, where a top-1000 university is worth 3 points). There is NO GMAT or GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance). There is NO startup-project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, 30 points). There is NO summa cum laude bonus and NO further-language bonus (Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance, +2 and +10 respectively). There is NO extracurricular-activities bonus (a bachelor-level instrument). There is also no scored credit for the prestige, class or grade of the previous degree.

The practical consequence: 100% of the score is generated by four things the applicant produces specifically for this application — the CV, the portfolio, the two-page project proposal and the fifteen-minute interview. A graduate of an unranked university with a mediocre transcript is not penalised at all, and a graduate of a famous school gains nothing automatically. For a Turkish or other international applicant this is unusually favourable: the entire competitive effort should go into the dossier, not into credentials that cannot be changed.
portfolio_and_materials:
THREE SCORED SUBMISSIONS, all uploaded in the application portal by the application deadline, all in English.

1. CURRICULUM VITAE — in English, PDF, max 20 points. No page or character limit is published. Scored on 'the consistence of the previous academic career with the contents of the course and significant experiences not included in academic training', so non-academic creative practice should be included deliberately, not omitted as irrelevant.

2. PORTFOLIO — in English, PDF, MAXIMUM FILE SIZE 20 MB, max 20 points. No page limit is published — the only hard constraint is the 20 MB cap, which for an image-heavy art/design portfolio means compressing images before export. Scored on: consistence of the projects with the contents of the course; observational and judgment skills; innovative and creative thinking; and 'Formal qualities of the portfolio in relation to artistic and design production' — i.e. the design of the portfolio document itself is graded, not only the work inside it.

3. OUTLINE OF A PROJECT PROPOSAL — PDF, MAXIMUM TWO A4 PAGES, max 20 points. This is a set brief, not an open statement of purpose, and it is quoted here in full because answering the wrong question is the commonest way to lose these 20 points: 'To assess your interest in the programme, we invite you to submit an outline of a project proposal. This exercise aims to understand your awareness of the subjects taught and your ability to connect them in a coherent and meaningful way. What are the most pressing issues that, in your view, should be considered by practitioners in the field of art or design working at the intersection of culture and technology? What answers should be provided to the urgent questions that the present confronts us with? In a maximum of two A4 pages, we expect you: to explain the core ideas of your project via an abstract describing the context in which the project is positioned and the topics that will be addressed; to visualise it concisely with the help of images (these can include graphics, explicative diagrams, references, sketches, etc.) that will enable us to understand how the project could be formalised. We are not looking for fully developed projects but for compelling ideas that demonstrate your thought process and creativity.' Note that IMAGES ARE REQUIRED, not optional — a text-only proposal fails half the brief.

EXPLICIT AI PROHIBITION, unusual among unibz programmes and quoted verbatim: 'We are very interested in the candidates' motivation and their ability to communicate it, which is why it is very important that artificial intelligence is not used in the drafting of this document.' It is stated as an expectation rather than as a sanctioned rule, but the interview is designed to probe exactly the ideas in the proposal, so a candidate cannot safely submit text they cannot defend live.

HARD EXCLUSION RULE, and note its asymmetry: 'Failure to upload the curriculum vitae and the outline of a project proposal by the deadlines will result in the exclusion from the admission procedure.' The portfolio is NOT named in that sentence — so omitting the portfolio is apparently not an automatic exclusion, but it forfeits 20 of the 60 Stage 1 points and makes the 30/60 gate nearly unreachable. Treat all three as mandatory.

NOT REQUIRED: no motivation letter, no video, no reference letters, no research proposal beyond the two-page outline, no writing sample, no interview-stage portfolio resubmission (though 'if deemed appropriate, candidates may use material documenting personal interests and/or previous experiences' during the interview). There is also NO study-career Excel template of the kind the Faculty of Economics and Engineering masters require.
interview:
YES — a compulsory second stage, worth 40 of the 100 points, and the single heaviest element in the whole procedure. Only candidates who reach 30/60 in Stage 1 are invited. Format: online, 'lasting approximately 15 minutes', described as 'a dialogue to gain a deeper understanding on the candidate's ideas, experiences and points of view'.

PUBLISHED 2026/27 INTERVIEW DATES (all online, all programme-specific): EARLY BIRD 21/05/2026 = 2026-05-21; LATE APPLICATION 21/07/2026 = 2026-07-21; ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION 15/09/2026 = 2026-09-15. Each falls a few days before the corresponding ranking-list publication date (27/05, 23/07 and 18/09 respectively), so the turnaround between interview and result is under a week and candidates should keep the date free.

EVALUATION CRITERIA: 'Interdisciplinary interest; Communication skills; Creative abilities of the candidates.' TOPICS COVERED: 'Portfolio, curriculum vitae, and project proposal (if deemed appropriate, candidates may use material documenting personal interests and/or previous experiences); General questions on topics related to design and/or art in relation to the specifics of the programme; Experience already acquired in the field of study; Inter- and transdisciplinary experiences; Innovative and creative thinking; Ability to discuss and reflect critically.'

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS 40% WEIGHT SUGGESTS: it is also the FIRST tie-break criterion, ahead of the portfolio and CV. And because the interview interrogates the submitted project proposal, it functions as an authenticity check on the documents — which is consistent with the programme's explicit request that AI not be used to draft the proposal. Two 2026/27 admits at exactly 60/100 and a documented case of an applicant moving from 22/60 at Stage 1 to 72/100 overall in the next session show that interview performance can decide the outcome outright.
conditional_admission:
THREE conditional regimes, and one of them is unusually generous.

(1) NOT YET GRADUATED — NO MINIMUM ECTS THRESHOLD. Quoted in full: 'If you have not yet graduated at the time of application: You can apply, but you will be admitted conditionally and need to submit your diploma by the enrolment deadline.' The only documentary requirement is 'if not graduated yet: please upload the list of your passed exams'. This is a genuine and checkable difference from the rest of unibz: most masters require at least 120 acquired ECTS to apply conditionally and the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance requires 140, and both require a structured Excel confirmation file. Neither the 120/140 threshold nor the Excel template appears anywhere in the CCP admission documents. A final-year student can therefore apply on the strength of a transcript alone. The Late Application list shows one such admit — Applicant ID 119805, rank 3 with 74 points, marked with the asterisk: 'applicants who have not concluded their bachelor's degree are provisionally admitted: requirement for admission is the conclusion of the bachelor studies by the enrolment deadline (13 October 2026, 12 midday).'

IF YOU GRADUATE LATE: 'You cannot enrol and you will lose your place, which will be offered to the subsequent applicant in the ranking list. In this case you should not pay the tuition fees to secure your admission. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there still are available places, you can enrol by 11 December 2026' (2026-12-11). The advice not to pay first is unibz's own, and matters because the first instalment is otherwise non-refundable.

(2) QUALIFICATION GAINED ABROAD — RESERVATION UNTIL VERIFIED. 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified.' And from the decree: 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' Even after enrolment: 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'

(3) NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD are provisionally admitted as an entire class: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' All five non-EU admits in the 2026/27 Early Bird list carry this reservation.
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE — no OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) mechanism exists for this programme, and none is mentioned in the admission-information PDF, the brochure, the programme page or either signed ranking list. OFA is an Italian undergraduate instrument, assigned at unibz to bachelor candidates who fail the compulsory mathematics test (Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics, Tourism Sport and Event Management). At master level the equivalent quality control happens entirely BEFORE admission, here through three pre-admission gates: the disciplinary eligibility check (a qualifying degree class, an Accademia/ISIA first-level diploma, or 12 credit points in the listed fields, with 'A commission checks the validity and equivalence of the credit points'); the English B2 language requirement; and the two scoring thresholds of 30/60 at Stage 1 and 60/100 overall. No admitted candidate carries a remedial obligation in either 2026/27 ranking list. The only post-admission obligations of any kind are curricular rather than remedial: the mandatory safety training that gates access to the technical workshops, and the mandatory 3 CP Italian or German language course in year 2.
language_requirements:
A SINGLE REQUIREMENT: ENGLISH AT B2. Quoted in full from the admission-information PDF: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) — English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.' Both signed ranking-list decrees restate it in one line: 'To be admitted you must fulfil the language requirements: English: B2.' No Italian, no German, no second or third language, and no exit level is published anywhere in the programme's documentation.

HOW PROOF IS SUBMITTED: 'You can demonstrate your language proficiency in the application portal (in the section "upload language certificates" and/or "enrol for language exams") after you have created an application in the section "create/manage applications".' Administrative distinction, quoted: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.' The proof must be in place by the application deadline; certificates that cannot be uploaded 'can be sent by e-mail as PDF files or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline'.

WHAT COUNTS AS SATISFYING B2. Because the two prior-qualification routes are recognised at C1, they clear the B2 bar with a level to spare: the main teaching language of the final high-school year, if English, is recognised as C1, and a bachelor or master degree taught in English is recognised as C1. For an applicant from Türkiye or a similar system, an English-medium bachelor is therefore normally sufficient on its own, provided the medium of instruction is documented: 'If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.'

ENFORCEMENT IN PRACTICE (2026/27): only two applicants in the entire cycle were excluded for failing the language requirement, both in the Early Bird EU pool (Applicant IDs 154425 and 131067), and the decree notes 'They may re-apply in the second session.' The Late list records no separate language-exclusion table, only the general closing line that unlisted applicants 'were excluded from the admission procedure because they did not meet the admission requirements (language requirement or study title)'. By unibz standards this is a very low language-attrition rate and confirms that the language gate is not the binding constraint on this programme.

AFTER ADMISSION: the study plan contains one mandatory 3 CP 'Language Course (Italian or German)' in the second year, with the rule 'Students must choose one of the two language courses offered, other than the language of the highschool diploma.' Language Centre courses are free of charge, and pre-sessional intensive courses run every September, with beginner (A1) modules 'offered exclusively during the pre-sessional September session' and 'never offered during the academic year' — relevant to anyone intending to start Italian or German from zero.
entry_levels_by_position:
B2 / none / none. In unibz's positional notation — where the 1st language is the one the candidate is strongest in, the 2nd the next and the 3rd the weakest — this programme sets a requirement only in the FIRST position, and that position must be filled by English specifically. There is no 2nd-language requirement and no 3rd-language requirement, because there is only one teaching language.

Comparison across unibz, to place this correctly: Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance and Master in Accounting and Finance C1/B2/none (trilingual, two languages compulsory); Bachelor in Computer Science B2/B2/none; Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering B2/B1/none; Master in Computing for Data Science B2/none/none; MASTER IN CRITICAL CREATIVE PRACTICES B2/none/none. It therefore sits at the most permissive end of the unibz scale, tied with the other English-only masters.

FOR A TYPICAL TURKISH APPLICANT: English occupies the only relevant position and is normally satisfied at C1 by an English-medium bachelor or an English-medium high school, or at B2 by a recognised certificate — IELTS Academic or General 5.5-6.5, TOEFL iBT 72-94, Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, PTE Academic 59-75, LanguageCert B2, telc English B2, Aptis ESOL General or Advanced B2, Michigan MET B2 in all four skills, Oxford Test of English B2, or UNIcert Level II. Anything at C1 or above (IELTS 7.0-8.0, TOEFL iBT 95-113, Cambridge C1 Advanced, PTE Academic 76-84) obviously also satisfies B2. NOTE that unibz recognises IELTS, TOEFL, TOEIC and the LanguageCert Academic and ESOL Access lines as 'home edition' variants, which matters for candidates who cannot reach a test centre — see certificate_rules. Italian and German are irrelevant to admission at every stage.
exit_levels:
NONE PUBLISHED. Unlike unibz's trilingual degrees, whose admission documents carry an explicit 'Exit level (to graduate)' line (typically C1/C1/B1), the Master in Critical Creative Practices admission-information PDF contains no exit-level section at all: the 'Language requirements' section lists only 'Entry level (to gain admission) — English: B2' and then moves to the proof pathways. Neither signed ranking-list decree, nor the brochure, nor the programme page mentions a graduation language requirement.

The only language obligation standing between an admitted student and the degree is CURRICULAR, not certificational: the mandatory 3 CP 'Language Course (Italian or German)' in the second year, which 'Students must choose ... other than the language of the highschool diploma.' It is a credit-bearing course to attend and pass like any other, not a CEFR level to certify at a Language Centre exam.

[uncertain] — no unibz document states positively that there is NO exit language requirement; the conclusion rests on the absence of the exit-level clause that unibz prints in every trilingual programme's admission PDF, plus the absence of any such clause in the two signed decrees, plus the fact that the study plan's only language element is the 3 CP course. Likewise, no published document states which CEFR level the 3 CP course targets or is assessed at. An applicant for whom this is decisive should confirm with the Faculty Secretariat (design-art@unibz.it, +39 0471 015000) or the Language Centre (language.centre@unibz.it) before enrolling.
third_language_exam_threshold: NOT APPLICABLE. There is no third language in this programme, so the unibz rule that 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language' has nothing to bite on. Every curricular course in the 2026/27 offering is taught and examined in English, so no examination is gated behind an Italian or German level, and no placement test in a third language is imposed after admission. The 3 CP Italian-or-German language course in year 2 is itself the language provision, delivered by the Language Centre at whatever level the student is placed in, and it carries no published B1 prerequisite. This is one of the clearest structural differences between this programme and the trilingual unibz degrees, where the B1 third-language gate can block a student from sitting compulsory courses.
proof_pathways:
FOUR RECOGNISED WAYS TO PROVE ENGLISH B2, all handled inside the application portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup/ after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'.

(1) MAIN TEACHING LANGUAGE OF THE FINAL HIGH-SCHOOL YEAR, if English — 'recognised as C1'. Foreign qualifications: 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' Related permanent recognitions in Resolution 16/2026: IGCSE and GCSE qualifications containing A levels, and International Baccalaureate Diploma programmes taught in English, are treated as secondary school diplomas with English as predominant language of instruction; IB subject grades are also mapped individually (for example English B HL grade 5 or 6, or English A Language and Literature SL grade 3, map to the intermediate bands).

(2) A BACHELOR OR MASTER DEGREE TAUGHT IN ENGLISH — 'recognised as C1'. 'unibz graduates must upload the language certificates obtained and/or declare that they have passed language exams at the unibz Language Centre (B2, B2+ or C1).' Foreign qualifications: 'If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' This is the standard and cheapest route for a graduate of an English-medium programme and comfortably exceeds the B2 requirement.

(3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official list (Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026). B2 English options include: Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, B2 First for Schools grade B or C, B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage) grade B or C, and C1 Advanced (CAE) at level B2; Michigan MET B2 in all four skills and ECCE; TOEFL iBT 72-94 and TOEIC Listening 400+/Reading 385+/Speaking 160+/Writing 150+; IELTS (General and Academic) 5.5-6.5; Aptis ESOL General B2 and Aptis ESOL Advanced B2; PTE Academic 59-75, PTE General Level 3, PEIC B2; LanguageCert General B2, Academic B2, ESOL B2; Oxford Test of English B2; telc English B2; UNIcert Level II English; IGCSE/GCSE English as a second language grade A, B or C. 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.'

(4) A LANGUAGE EXAM ORGANISED BY THE UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE, registered through the portal under 'enrol for language exams'. 2026/27 sessions, all online: Early Bird 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026, marked FULLY BOOKED on the Language Centre page) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late Application 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). SEQUENCING TRAP, quoted: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' TWO FURTHER LIMITS: 'It is not possible to take exams at different levels for the same language'; and, decisively for the session that is open at the verification date, 'Applicants in the Additional and Super Late Application Session (where foreseen) can only certify their language skills for admission by submitting a language certificate recognised by unibz (unibz language exams are not available)' — so anyone applying in the 18/08-04/09/2026 window must already hold a certificate or a qualifying English-medium diploma. Compensatory measures (extra time, additional IT tools) are available for candidates with a disability certificate submitted to Student Support no later than the exam registration deadline.
certificate_rules:
Governed by the Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026 — 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants' — a trilingual German/Italian/English document published at https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf and linked directly from the programme page.

GENERAL DISPOSITIONS, quoted from the English column. To be recognised, a certificate must '1. include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself' and '2. indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade (and/or the detailed assessment is indicated on the certificate itself or by appropriate documentation faithful to the original by the certification organisation)'. Further binding rules: 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed' — the WEAKEST sub-skill sets the level, so a candidate with three B2 bands and one B1 band certifies B1, not B2; 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation'; 'Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations will not be accepted' — a certificate cannot be assembled from several providers; 'Certificates of participation, certificates of end-of-course-tests and examinations from private educational institutions as well as results of placement tests will not be recognised'; 'Certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff will not be recognised'; 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.'

VALIDITY: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January' — i.e. a certificate issued from 1 January of the fifth preceding year stays valid for the whole of the current year. Certificates listed in the 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' section (school-leaving and university qualifications, IB, IGCSE/GCSE with A levels) have UNLIMITED validity, which is why the English-medium-degree route is the most durable one.

HOME EDITION: 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list.' In the English table the exception marker '* Also accepted as "home edition"' is attached at provider level to TOEFL and TOEIC (ETS), IELTS (British Council), and the LanguageCert Academic and ESOL Access lines. For an applicant who cannot reach a physical test centre, an at-home IELTS or TOEFL iBT is therefore the safest option; other providers' at-home variants are not covered. Confirm any borderline case with language.centre@unibz.it before paying for a test.

application_deadline_non_eu:
ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. They are ranked on a separate list against a separate quota of 5 places, and after admission must pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT WITHOUT AN ITALIAN RESIDENCE PERMIT: exactly one attempt per academic year, closing at the end of April — five months before teaching starts — for 5 places, with the online interview on 21/05/2026 and the result by 27/05/2026. In the 2026/27 cycle 21 non-EU applicants were ranked and 5 admitted, with the last two admitted sitting exactly on the 60-point floor. Missing the April window means waiting a full year; there is no second chance in the same cycle, and the €50 fee is non-refundable.
parity_of_treatment:
Two categories are treated as EU applicants, and the second is the one that matters most to Turkish and other non-EU nationals already in Italy. Quoted: 'Considered as equivalent are: 1. Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; 2. Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay.' EXPLICIT EXCLUSION: 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid.' If the permit has expired, a renewal request must be attached. CRITICAL WARNING, quoted: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The signed Early Bird decree restates it: 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998) you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.'

WHY THIS IS WORTH MORE HERE THAN AT ALMOST ANY OTHER UNIBZ PROGRAMME. The two pools behaved in opposite ways in 2026/27. The EU/parity pool was UNDERSUBSCRIBED: 8 admitted against 20 Early Bird places, 9 more in the Late session, 17 in total against 30 EU places, and a third session had to be opened in August. The non-EU pool was FULL AND BRUTAL: 5 places, 5 admitted, 21 ranked, cut-off exactly on the 60-point floor, and no second or third session available. A qualifying applicant who fails to upload the permit therefore loses access to a pool where places went spare, loses two extra application sessions, loses the right to re-apply after a weak first attempt, and additionally pays the €50 fee. Establishing parity of treatment is the single highest-value administrative step available to an eligible applicant for this programme.
places_quotas:
THREE separate quotas for 2026/27, published in the admission-information PDF as: 'Available places — EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: Early Bird Application: 20; Late Application: 10. Non-EU citizens (living abroad): Early Bird Application: 5.' The 'At a glance' box on the programme page and the brochure summarises the same allocation as 'Places available: 30 EU + 5 non-EU' (30 = 20 + 10). The EU:non-EU ratio is 6:1. CARRY-OVER RULE: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' Unfilled EU places are never transferred to the non-EU pool, and the non-EU quota exists only in the Early Bird session.

ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE, from the two signed ranking lists. EARLY BIRD: 8 EU/parity admitted against 20 places — 12 places unfilled and carried into the Late session; 8 further EU applicants failed Stage 1 and 2 were excluded on language. Non-EU: 5 admitted against 5 places — the quota exactly filled, with 5 more applicants scoring 36-51 below the 60 floor and 11 more failing Stage 1. LATE APPLICATION: 9 EU/parity admitted (against 10 nominal late places plus the 12 carried over, so still short), with 1 applicant excluded at 30 points. RUNNING TOTAL: 17 EU/parity and 5 non-EU admitted, i.e. 22 of the 35 published places taken across the two closed sessions.

That shortfall is precisely why the ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION was opened for this programme. Its ranking list is due by 18/09/2026 and did not exist at the verification date, so the exact number of places still on offer is not published — but roughly 13 EU places were unclaimed after the Late session, and the Faculty opening the session at all confirms places remained. For an EU or parity-of-treatment applicant this is an unusually favourable supply-demand position; for a non-EU applicant living abroad it is irrelevant, because that session is closed to them.

required_documents:
AT APPLICATION, via the portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup/ :
(1) AN ACCOUNT plus a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'.
(2) THE COMPLETED AND CORRECTLY SUBMITTED ONLINE FORM — 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.'
(3) ACADEMIC BACKGROUND. If graduated in Italy: 'diploma supplement or substitute-declaration (following the Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000) of the degree awarded, final grade, exams passed with corresponding grade, the dates in which the exams were passed, the credit points, the subject areas, and the teaching hours'. If graduated abroad: 'diploma supplement or final degree certificate issued by the foreign university (to be translated into English if in a language other than Italian, German or English) detailing the final mark, exams passed as well as corresponding grades, the dates in which the exams were passed, the credit points, and the teaching hours. A description of the contents of single courses is recommended; it is advisable to attach a declaration of value or similar document by the university with the indication of the lowest grade needed in order to achieve the degree as well as the highest mark obtainable'. If not graduated yet: 'please upload the list of your passed exams'. NOTE the translation rule is into ENGLISH at application stage (Italian is required only for the degree diploma at enrolment), and that TEACHING HOURS are explicitly demanded — many foreign transcripts omit them, so request a supplementary letter from the home university.
(4) CURRICULUM VITAE in English, PDF (scored, max 20 points).
(5) PORTFOLIO in English, PDF, maximum 20 MB (scored, max 20 points).
(6) OUTLINE OF A PROJECT PROPOSAL, PDF, maximum two A4 pages, including images (scored, max 20 points).
(7) PROOF OF ENGLISH B2 — a recognised certificate uploaded under 'upload language certificates', or a high-school/university medium-of-instruction document, or registration for a Language Centre exam under 'enrol for language exams'.
(8) IF THE QUALIFICATION WAS GAINED ABROAD, the diploma of the qualification — 'if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'.
(9) FOR NON-EU CITIZENS RESIDENT IN ITALY CLAIMING PARITY OF TREATMENT, a copy of the valid permit to stay, plus a renewal request if it has expired.
There is NO study-career Excel template for this programme. 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.'

AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign university degree must additionally upload: the degree diploma of the Bachelor; 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)'; and the Diploma Supplement, 'where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. Then the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements appropriate to the country (see credential_recognition). Students transferring from another Italian university 'must submit to the Student Office - at the beginning of the academic year - a copy of the transfer application presented at the university of provenance'. Non-EU students must hand the residence permit in at the Student Office in person or by e-mail once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable ONLY by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. Quoted from the admission-information PDF, section 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy)': 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' unibz's parallel guidance for this group describes it as an administration fee and states that it is non-refundable: 'The application fee is 50€. Given that the non-EU pool for this programme has 5 places and admitted 5 of 21 ranked applicants in 2026/27, the fee buys a single, genuinely competitive attempt; establishing parity of treatment where legitimately available removes both the fee and the bottleneck.

credential_recognition:
At enrolment, holders of a foreign university degree must upload the Bachelor degree diploma, 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)', and the Diploma Supplement showing 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. Then, depending on the foreign education system: (a) EU COUNTRIES, SWITZERLAND, NORWAY, ICELAND, LIECHTENSTEIN — a 'Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database – Italy'; (b) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a 'Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA)'; (c) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE NOT SIGNATORIES OF THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA.

'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents.' From the signed decree: 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' And: 'Please note that if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'

TÜRKİYE is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence PLUS CIMEA Statement of Verification. Both must be in hand by the 13/10/2026 enrolment deadline; CIMEA verification carries a fee and a processing time of several weeks, so it should be started as soon as the ranking list is published — for an Early Bird non-EU admit that means from late May, not from October.

NOTE THE SPLIT OF RESPONSIBILITIES, which is different from the ECO masters. At APPLICATION stage the eligibility check on the 12 credit points in Design, Architecture, Arts, Museology, Cinema, Photography, Media Studies or Philosophy is made by the Faculty's own commission on the transcript itself — 'A commission checks the validity and equivalence of the credit points' — which is why the transcript must show credit points AND teaching hours, and why 'A description of the contents of single courses is recommended'. ARDI/CIMEA recognition is a separate, ENROLMENT-stage requirement. A candidate whose transcript uses an unusual credit system, or whose art-school subjects have no obvious Italian counterpart, should attach course descriptions and a declaration of value at application stage rather than relying on ARDI/CIMEA later.

Separately: 'Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.' Links: https://ardi.cimea.it/en ; https://cimea-diplome.it/page-comparability-verification-service ; https://cimea-diplome.it/page-verification-service ; signatory list https://www.enic-naric.net/
